newsitem.title: USA: Integrity sets writedown, sees year loss.
newsitem.headline: Integrity sets writedown, sees year loss.

text.p: Integrity Inc said Wednesday its fourth-quarter and full-year 1996 results will include an accounting adjustment of $2.7 million, or $0.49 per share, related to a non-cash writedown of a building project and record masters.

It said the writedown is expected to result in a net loss for the year of between $2.9 million and $3.3 million, or between $0.53 and $0.60 per share. In 1995, Integrity posted a loss of $2.1 million or $0.37 per share.
Chairman P. Michael Coleman said in a statement that the accounting adjustment should enable Integrity to enter the new year with a realistic market-based value for these assets.

The building project, a 44,000-square-foot headquarters expansion, began in early 1995 and was halted due to general business conditions. Coleman said no suitable tenant has been found for the building, which accounts for about $1.2 million of the writedown.
Record masters not expected to recoup recording costs, plus related inventory and supplies, make up the other component of the non-cash writedown.
Integrity produces and publishes Christian music.
